commits.message:
[CI] add presmoke for CI (#21685)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds a PR-scoped, on-demand **presmoke** image build, so a broken base
image
is caught before merge instead of waiting for (or hiding inside) the
full
nightly smoke run.

Context: when CANN-related content in the root Dockerfiles changes (CANN
base
image version, torch_npu / CANN alignment, dependency pins), the full
nightly
run is too heavy and too late to tell whether the image itself is
broken.
Presmoke builds exactly the images a PR would produce and nothing else,
on
demand, right on the PR.

Triggered by comment only (no new trigger, no label):
- `/presmoke <chips>` — build the nightly images only (no tests) for the
given
  chips, where `<chips>` is `a2`, `a3`, `310p`, `a5` or `all`.
- `/nightly <tests> --presmoke` — run the named tests against the images
  previously published by `/presmoke`.

Implemented in `pr_nightly_command.yml` (repository_dispatch): the chip
list is
taken directly from the command, with no inference from use cases/test
names.
Because comment-triggered workflows always resolve from the default
branch,
this adds no new trigger and leaves nightly and other scheduled builds
untouched. `docs/source/developer_guide/contribution/nightly_ci_test.md`
documents the new command.

### What it adds

- **Reuse, no duplicated build logic.**
`schedule_nightly_image_build_with_base.yaml`
  composes the existing building blocks per (chip, OS) pair through
  `_schedule_nightly_pair_image_build.yaml`:
  `build-base` (`_schedule_image_build.yaml`) -> `build-nightly`
  (`_nightly_image_build.yaml`).

- **One new `isolated_build` flag (plus `source_ref`) drives everything
  isolation-related**, so the isolation facets cannot be half-configured
(per review feedback the former per-facet inputs were collapsed into
this
  single boolean):
- Repositories: presmoke images go to the isolated
`ascend/vllm-ascend-presmoke`
and `base_image/ascend-ci/vllm-ascend-presmoke` repositories and never
    overwrite nightly images. Tags are unchanged.
- Full-scale: builds are always full (ubuntu + openEuler, amd64 +
arm64),
    including the openEuler variants.
- Never published: presmoke images are never pushed to
`atlas_inference`, and
    the quay.io and `swr.cn-north-4` syncs are skipped.

- **`source_ref` = `refs/pull/<n>/head` — pre-merge build.** Both layers
build
  the whole source tree from the PR head, so the code, Dockerfiles and
dependency pins under review are exactly what gets built; the branch
still
decides the published tag. `/presmoke` always pre-merges (it is not
limited to
  Dockerfile changes).

- **Test consumption.** `/nightly <tests> --presmoke` pulls the
`-presmoke`
repositories under the standard tag (via `image_repo_suffix=-presmoke`).

- **Concurrency.** Presmoke runs are guarded by a concurrency group with
`cancel-in-progress: true` (same pattern as `pr_test.yaml`), so
re-triggering
`/presmoke` cancels the previous presmoke build instead of stacking
builds.

SWR push is for triage, not for release: the images let a failing
presmoke run
be reproduced and debugged against the exact image it built. They live
only
under the `*-presmoke` repositories and are not part of any
release/publish path.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No. This is CI-only (GitHub Actions). It does not change the library
API,
runtime behavior, or any user-facing configuration. The only
user-visible
additions are the new `/presmoke` command and the documented
`--presmoke`
option for `/nightly`.

## How was this patch tested?

- CI: exercised by running `/presmoke <chips>` on a PR and, via
`workflow_dispatch`, on same-repository branches; `/nightly <tests>
--presmoke`
  consumes the published images.
- The pipeline reuses the already-tested `_schedule_image_build.yaml`
and
`_nightly_image_build.yaml`; both new inputs default to the standard
behavior,
  so existing nightly callers are unchanged.
- All modified workflow YAML is validated and `bash format.sh ci`
passes.

---------

commits.comment: 针对 vllm_ascend/ops/triton/sharded_indexer.py 的 kernel 级性能改造，服务的是 context-parallel/DCP 的 sharded indexer 在 pack_local_candidates 里的候选预处理（不是 attention 后端本身，但处于 DCP/QLI 的数据准备路径上，影响 attention 侧候选交换前的准备开销）。实现要点：删除原先「BF16 走基数排序 / FP32 走 _sort_candidate_pairs 比较交换」的分叉，统一为一个内联 LSD 基数排序循环，用 SCORE_BITS 这个 constexpr 区分 16(BF16)/32(FP32)，因此 dtype 选择不再带每行分支；digit 与当前 position 打包进 FP32（BLOCK=2048 时 11 位 position 标签，剩 13 位 digit），每次 pass 都是值排序 + gather，保证稳定；key 语义为 [降序 score key | 升序 local ID]，负零归一化但保留原始 payload，FP32 不做 BF16 舍入；同时把 ROWS 改成 do_not_specialize 的 num_rows、把 *ROW/*COL 改名为 *_STRIDE，减少重编译变体。关键行为变更：本地 token ID 由「逐行最大值归约 + short/full 宽度选择 + 大 ID 比较回退」改为固定 20-bit 字段，删除了所有回退路径，并在文档里声明「调用方必须保证 0 <= local_idx < 2**20」，wrapper 完全不做运行时校验——越界 ID 会被静默截断/排序错位，而不是报错；另外 wrapper 现在对非 BF16/FP32 分数直接抛 TypeError（此前 fp16 等会落入 FP32 路径被当作 FP32 处理），这是一个潜在的调用方兼容性变化。收益方面 PR 给出 A3 FP32 核内约 4.1–4.3x、A5 BF16 约 1.03–1.04x，完整 pack_local_candidates 路径约 1.2–2.5x，属实测可信但仅限该 kernel/预处理路径。风险判断为 medium：输出 schema 不变、排序语义（分数降序、ID 升序、稳定）被保留，但支持域被收窄且无兜底，任何越过 2**20 或使用非 BF16/FP32 分数的旧调用点都会静默或显式失败；此外 fuse 仍只在 K=2048 + 占用率/合并层级门槛满足时启用，其它 workload 继续走原生路径，行为分叉需要保持关注。

test_impact.reason: 本 commit 已新增 tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_candidate_radix.py 并把 test_dcp_candidates.py 的用例从 1<<24 改为 2**20-1，覆盖 BF16/FP32、列 stride 1/2、tie、signed zero、相邻分数、非法/非有限候选、radix digit 边界、最大 local ID、全局 ID 映射、非法 dtype 与 graph replay 输入变化；但新增的 20-bit 输入契约为调用方保证、kernel 无越界兜底，且删除大 ID 回退与 fp16 静默路径都需要在调用方（DCP/QLI 构图侧）补契约测试，故仍需扩展测试面。

commits.message:
[Performance][Kernel] Share exact radix sorting across BF16 and FP32 candidate packing (#21584)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Replace the FP32 compare/exchange sort in fused candidate packing with
the stable radix implementation shared by BF16 and FP32. The shared
operator is called by the context-parallel sharded indexer through
`pack_local_candidates`; this change optimizes candidate preparation
before merging, without adding a model-specific entry point.

Inputs are INT32 local token IDs and BF16/FP32 scores with shape `[T, 1,
K]`. The fused path uses **K = 2048** and returns INT32 `[T, K, 2]`
pairs containing the global token ID and the FP32 score payload.
Candidates are ordered by score descending, then token ID ascending.

The implementation uses one inline least-significant-digit radix loop:

- Valid local token IDs use a fixed **20-bit** field.
- Each pass sorts `digit * 2048 + position`. The 11-bit position tag
preserves the order established by earlier passes, leaving 13 digit bits
within FP32's 24-bit significand.
- BF16 uses 16 score-key bits and three passes; FP32 uses all 32
score-key bits and four passes.
- Scores and IDs follow the same permutation after every pass. Signed
zeros compare equal while retaining their original payloads; FP32 scores
are not rounded to BF16.

Remove the per-row maximum-ID reduction, short/full ID-width selection,
and large-ID radix fallback. Keep the comparison helper used by merge
kernels. Existing workload-based fused dispatch and the separate
sorting/packing path for other workloads remain in place.

The operator document and release note are included. Naming, contract
documentation, and specialization notes follow the guidance proposed in
#21201.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The intended change is lower FP32 candidate-packing latency while
preserving exact ordering and packed payloads within the declared input
contract.

**Callers must guarantee `0 <= local_id < 2**20` about 1M for valid
local token IDs.** This is the token index within a rank before global
mapping, not the position in the 2048-candidate array. Negative IDs
remain invalid sentinels. The wrapper does not perform a runtime range
check, and the fused kernel has no out-of-range fallback.

The wrapper accepts BF16 and FP32 scores and raises `TypeError` for
other score dtypes before allocation or launch. Invalid IDs and
non-finite scores produce invalid packed candidates. The output schema
is unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Validation applies to the current code at
`d42d39bad382bc92cb3124f8411eddc61fe138a0`.

- Focused Ruff lint/format, Python compilation, and whitespace checks
passed.
- The candidate-radix and existing candidate-pipeline test modules
passed on NPU. The independent CPU stable-sort reference checks exact
packed IDs and FP32 score bits.
- Coverage includes BF16/FP32, column strides 1/2, ties, signed zero,
adjacent scores, invalid/non-finite candidates, radix digit boundaries,
the maximum supported local ID `2**20 - 1`, mapped global IDs,
unsupported dtypes, and changed-input graph replay.
- Paired A3 FP32 and A5 BF16 profiling results are summarized below; raw
reports remain local.
- Full repository checks and model quality evaluation are not
established by these focused tests.

Reproduce the correctness checks in an installed NPU environment:

```bash
pytest -q tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_candidate_radix.py
pytest -q tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_dcp_candidates.py
```

**JIT specialization:** `num_rows` is runtime and marked
`do_not_specialize`. `SCORE_BITS` is selected by the wrapper to compile
the three- or four-pass loop. Strides, world size, rank, interleave, and
block size remain constexpr and can create distinct variants when their
values change; pointer dtype and alignment can also affect
specialization. This PR does not claim that all shapes share one
compiled kernel. Startup/serving compilation counts have not been
established by a dedicated workload audit. No new kernel or warmup
registration is introduced.

### Performance: paired kernel measurements

Measured on 2026-11-13 against frozen main
`6385299e417741fc576c30c95f7860fd69dbec24`. Candidate
`955894179886df79374aef0090a0b0b45b9e9fbe` applies the PR implementation
to that same baseline; the target module matches PR head
`d42d39bad382bc92cb3124f8411eddc61fe138a0`.

- A3 FP32: Ascend910_9362, 40 VectorCores. A5 BF16: Ascend950DT_9582, 64
VectorCores. Each comparison uses the same device and environment within
its platform.
- CANN 9.2.1, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, Triton-Ascend
3.6.0.post2.
- Inputs: `[T,1,2048]`, contiguous, WORLD=8, RANK=7, INTERLEAVE=768.
Valid local IDs span the 20-bit range, including `2**20-1`; fixed-seed
scores include ties, signed zeros, adjacent values, invalid IDs and
non-finite scores.
- Direct production `_pack_sorted_candidates` timing with `msprof op`,
warm-up=10 and launch-count=10, BasicInfo/PipeUtilization. Each
application explicitly invokes the kernel ten times; each case actually
produced ten official task rows. Values below are medians in
microseconds, not independent-process repetitions.
- All public-wrapper and direct-kernel checks passed against an
independent CPU oracle with exact packed IDs and score bits. All 320
official timing rows were retained.

| T (K=2048) | A3 FP32 main us | A3 FP32 PR us | Speedup | A5 BF16 main
us | A5 BF16 PR us | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 100.574 | 24.161 | 4.163x | 25.370 | 24.470 | 1.037x |
| 4 | 100.644 | 24.271 | 4.147x | 25.496 | 24.501 | 1.041x |
| 8 | 100.914 | 24.401 | 4.136x | 25.509 | 24.590 | 1.037x |
| 16 | 101.184 | 24.761 | 4.086x | 25.684 | 24.711 | 1.039x |
| 32 | 101.804 | 25.341 | 4.017x | 25.995 | 24.978 | 1.041x |
| 64 | 201.248 | 48.312 | 4.166x | 26.781 | 25.762 | 1.040x |
| 128 | 399.916 | 93.944 | 4.257x | 49.324 | 47.839 | 1.031x |
| 256 | 697.888 | 162.256 | 4.301x | 94.084 | 91.320 | 1.030x |

A separate A3 four-layer TP16/DCP16 run matched 352 rank/shape groups
for this kernel; group mean speedups ranged from 4.18x to 4.46x. This is
target-kernel evidence within a model run, not whole-model speedup or
end-to-end acceptance. Raw profiling artifacts remain local.

DCO metadata repair: PR head is now
`4e0915735257b25702f9c56754fa6a34eabcebdd`. All seven commit trees are
unchanged; the measurements above retain their original tested commit
IDs.

### Complete preparation path: native sort + pack versus fused radix

The comparison below measures the complete `pack_local_candidates`
preparation path, including allocation and dispatch, against frozen main
`6385299e417741fc576c30c95f7860fd69dbec24`. The fused path uses
candidate `955894179886df79374aef0090a0b0b45b9e9fbe`. The runner forces
the existing row/world workload gate off or on while preserving the
outer K, dtype and sort/fuse conditions. This is a comparison of
preparation paths, separate from the direct fused-kernel comparison
above.

Inputs are contiguous `[T,1,2048]`, with the same 20-bit ID contract and
exact CPU ordering/payload checks. Each path has 100 synchronized eager
wall samples per case, arranged in ten alternating AB/BA groups.
Compilation, warmup, transfers and reference checking are outside
timing. Values are medians in microseconds.

| W | T | A3 FP32 native us | A3 FP32 fused us | Speedup | A5 BF16
native us | A5 BF16 fused us | Speedup |

All 15 cases and all 150 paired group medians per platform favor fusion.
Each platform completed 730 exact CPU-oracle checkpoints across timed
and profiled applications. This supports removing the current workload
gates for the measured eager cases.

An unfiltered `msprof op` capture also includes every kernel in each
preparation call. Each profiled application makes ten complete calls
with per-call reference checks. The table reports the sum of official
task durations divided by ten; it excludes allocation and host
submission gaps and is a different timing boundary from eager wall
latency.

| Platform | W | T | Native kernels/call | Fused kernels/call | Native
total kernel us/call | Fused total kernel us/call |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A3 FP32 | 8 | 2 | 10 | 1 | 48.936 | 24.679 |
| A3 FP32 | 8 | 128 | 10 | 1 | 99.984 | 93.920 |
| A5 BF16 | 8 | 2 | 6 | 1 | 21.173 | 23.656 |
| A5 BF16 | 8 | 128 | 6 | 1 | 40.506 | 47.097 |

On A5, fusion increases summed device task time by 11.7% at T2 and 16.3%
at T128, while reducing complete eager latency through path
consolidation. The eager result does not establish a Graph replay
benefit. Graph performance remains unmeasured: the initial runner
checked capture output before its first replay. The current PR retains
its workload gates pending that comparison. W1 performance and other
dtype/platform combinations are outside this path-comparison matrix. Raw
samples, variation and the failed runner records remain local.

- [x] Functionality, production caller, input/output contract, and
operator documentation.
- [x] Exact ordering/payload checks and supported boundary coverage.
- [x] Unsupported score dtype rejection.
- [x] Focused lint, formatting, and correctness checks.
- [x] Specialization conditions and remaining recompilation risks
documented.
- [x] Paired A3 FP32 and A5 BF16 kernel validation and profiling.
- [x] Full repository CI.
- [ ] Model quality evaluation and end-to-end performance acceptance.

commits.comment: 补齐 310P Model Runner V2 的结构化输出能力，改动集中在 vllm_ascend/_310p/worker/v2/ 这一自包含的 310P 实现树，未触碰主平台的 NPUModelRunner/sampler/attention 抽象。实现方式：NPUModelRunner310V2.sample 先 compute_logits，再对 grammar_output 走新增的 apply_grammar_bitmask，替代原来的 NotImplementedError；apply_grammar_bitmask 用 Protocol 只声明 req_ids 与 cu_num_logits_np 两个字段，说明其依赖面被刻意收窄到 runner batch 元数据。核心算法在宿主侧完成：以 mask_stride = bitmask.shape[0] // len(structured_output_request_ids) 把 scheduler 顺序的定长 bitmask 行按 runner 顺序（req_id -> idx 映射 + cu_num_logits_np 的 [start,end) 区间）重排进全 -1 的 sorted_bitmask，天然支持「混合结构化/非结构化批次」与「不同 draft token 数」；随后在该 batch 上做 numpy 小端解包（unpackbits(bitorder='little')）并按 logits.shape[1] 截断以处理词表尾部不整字，最终把 bool 阻塞掩码 non_blocking 拷到 logits 设备并 masked_fill_(-inf)，全程不把 logits 拉回 host（只在 host 上搬运掩码），与 310P 无 Triton 的限制一致。语义上依赖 rejection sampler 在第一个 grammar 非法 draft 处截断（Greedy/概率采样均适用），因此不需要额外 acceptance bound。潜在风险：1) mask_stride 由整数除法推导，若 scheduler 对某请求给出的掩码行数与 end-start 不一致，多余行被丢弃、不足行补 -1（即全部屏蔽），行为依赖 vLLM GrammarOutput 的行布局约定，跨版本 vLLM 变更时是脆弱点；2) 逐 grammar 请求的 Python 循环 + numpy 解包是纯宿主开销，长批次/大词表(llm vocab 全量)下的 CPU 时间未做性能评估；3) sorted_bitmask 用 torch.full 默认 CPU dtype=int32 构造，依赖 logits 与 mask 的 dtype 约定，若上游 mask 变成 uint32/其它宽度需同步调整；4) 只在 sample 阶段应用 mask，若 310P MRV2 存在其它 sampling 入口（如 spec decode 的额外分支）需要确认都会被覆盖。功能上属明确的用户可见能力提升（310P MRV2 可用 JSON Schema/JSON object/regex/choice/grammar + MTP）。

commits.message:
[Feature][MRV2][310P] Support structured outputs for Model Runner V2 (#20360)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR enables structured outputs for the Ascend 310P Model Runner V2.
Previously, the 310P MRV2 path raised `NotImplementedError` when grammar
output was provided.

The implementation:

- Reorders the scheduler-provided grammar bitmask rows to match the
request order and per-request logit offsets used by the 310P model
runner.
- Handles mixed structured and unstructured batches, as well as requests
with different numbers of draft tokens.
- Unpacks the scheduler's packed grammar bitmask on the host and applies
the resulting blocked-token mask to logits in place on the logits
device.
- Relies on rejection sampling to stop at the first grammar-invalid MTP
draft for both greedy and probabilistic sampling.

The change is limited to structured-output correctness support in the
Ascend 310P MRV2 path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Ascend 310P MRV2 can now process structured-output requests using
JSON Schema, JSON object, regex, choice, and grammar constraints,
including supported MTP configurations.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests:

- `tests/ut/_310p/test_structured_outputs_v2_310p.py`

The new tests cover reordered grammar requests, mixed
structured/unstructured requests, variable draft lengths, bitmask sign
bits and vocabulary tails, empty grammar requests, non-MTP sampling, and
invalid-draft rejection under greedy and probabilistic sampling.

Testing `--structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"xgrammar"}'` results:
Json Schema
```
{
  "name": "Einstein",
  "birthday": "1879-03-14",
  "facts": [
    "physics",
    "relativity"
  ]
}
```
Json object
```
{
  "name": "Albert Einstein",
  "birthday": "1879-03-14",
  "facts": [
    "He developed the theory of relativity.",
    "He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.",
    "He was a Swiss-born theoretical physicist.",
    "He was known for his hair and his pacifist views."
  ]
}
```
---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.
